description: General vendor invoice and municipal bill extraction for vendor and city-issued billing documents.

vendor_name.description: Name of the company, supplier, contractor, tradesperson, service provider, utility, or vendor issuing the invoice and requesting payment. Usually appears near the logo, top header, remittance details, or vendor contact block. Do not return the customer, Invoice To party, Bill To party, property manager, property owner, tenant, attention line, technician, or contact person.

invoice_date.description: Date the invoice was issued. May be labeled Invoice Date, Date, Billing Date, Issue Date, Tax Invoice Date, Statement Date, or Notice Date. Return the issue date, not the due date, service date, or delivery date.

payment_due_date.description: Date payment is due. May be labeled Due Date, Payment Due Date, Payable By, Due On, or Balance Due Date. Return only an explicitly printed calendar date. Do not infer from invoice date, terms, or amount. If none is printed, return null.

invoice_number.description: Unique invoice identifier assigned by the vendor for this invoice. Prefer the value in the invoice header or top-right invoice table that is directly labeled Invoice #, Invoice No., Invoice Number, Inv #, Inv No., Tax Invoice No., Bill Number, or Document Number. The invoice number is often near the invoice date. If the document includes both an invoice page and a work order page, prefer the value labeled Invoice # on the invoice page; use a standalone '#:' value on the work order page only if it matches the invoice page number. Return only the identifier value, not the label. Do not return P.O. No., PO #, PO number, job number, work order number, project number, reference number, customer number, account number, vendor GST number, tax ID, phone number, postal code, license number, product registration number, date, subtotal, GST amount, total amount, balance due, or service address.

po_or_job_number.description: Purchase order, job, work order, project, or reference number. May be labeled PO #, P.O. No., Purchase Order, Job #, Job No., Job Number, Work Order, WO, Project No., Site Ref, Customer Ref, or Reference. If both PO and Job exist, return PO number only. Return null if none is present.

gst_amount.description: Canadian GST (5%) amount charged. Prefer the amount directly labeled GST, G.S.T., GST@5.0%, GST 5%, or Goods and Services Tax. Return the numeric amount, not the rate. If a separate provincial sales tax (PST) line is present, return only the GST line, not PST and not Total Tax. Use Total Tax only when there is no separate GST line and no other tax types are present. Do not return the GST registration number, subtotal, total, or balance due.

total_invoice_amount.description: Final amount the recipient must pay, including all taxes and charges. Prefer values labeled Total, Invoice Total, Amount Due, Balance Due, Total Due, Grand Total, Amount Payable, or Please Pay. If Total and Balance Due are both present and equal, return that amount. Do not return subtotal, GST, amount paid, or a line amount.

service_address.description: Address where the work, service, delivery, or billed property is located. Prefer Service Address, Service Location, Site Address, Job Address, Work Location, Property Address, Premises, Service For, or (for municipal bills) the assessed or billed property address. If both Bill To and a service/site address are present, return the service/site address. Do not return the vendor's own office address. Do not use the Bill To or mailing address.

bill_type.description:
Classify by WHO issued the document/invoice/bill and what kind of biller they are — never by who is being billed. Municipal bill is issued by a government or municipal body — a city, town, regional district, or municipal utility. Includes utility charges billed by a municipality (water, sewer, waste, stormwater), business license and permit renewal fees, and other city-issued charges.Commercial document or invoice is issued by a private business — tradespeople and contractors (plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing, carpentry, restoration, general contracting, appliance repair, pest control), grounds and landscaping services, fire inspection serivce, private utility providers (private power/gas/telecom companies), insurers, and general suppliers. Tie-breakers, in order:(1) Classify by the ISSUER, never the customer. A private contractor billing a city or municipality is 'commercial'. A municipality billing a landlord or property manager is 'municipal'.
(2) A utility billed by a MUNICIPALITY (city water/sewer/waste) is 'municipal'. The same kind of service billed by a PRIVATE company is 'commercial'.
(3) If you cannot confirm the issuer is a government body or a city or a municipality, output 'commercial'.

is_handwritten.description: Classify yes when any important field (vendor name, total amount, service address, GST amount, or PO/job number) appears handwritten or manually filled in. Classify no when those fields are printed or digitally generated, even if there are handwritten notes, signatures, or checkboxes elsewhere. This value is informational only.

invoice_description.description: One short sentence (15 words or fewer) describing what this invoic is for, from the line items, Service For, or notes. Do not include vendor name, numbers, address, date, tax, or total. Do not mention GST. Examples: 'Lawn maintenance service in March.' 'Electrical repair work.' 'Monthly water utility charges in June.' 'Annual business license renewal for 2026.' Return an empty string if undeterminable.

anomaly_flag.description: Note genuine anomalies for a reviewer: vendor name missing, total amount missing, a total amount lower than the GST amount when GST is present, a GST amount that is clearly not about 5% of the pre-tax amount when GST is present, a suspiciously round total with no itemisation, or duplicate-looking line items. Do not flag a missing invoice number or a missing payment due date. Return an empty string if nothing is unusual.
